subject: Oceanography
title: Plastic and Marine Life
description: A fast breakdown of Plastic and Marine Life for builders.

hook.text: Over 700 marine species interact with plastic debris—through ingestion, entanglement, or habitat alteration.

buildup.text: Sea turtles mistake plastic bags for jellyfish—seabirds feed bottle caps to their chicks.

discovery.text: 90% of seabirds now have plastic in their stomachs—up from 5% in 1960.

twist.text: Plastic doesn't just kill by choking—chemicals leaching from it disrupt hormones and weaken immune systems.

climax.text: On Midway Atoll, albatross chicks die with stomachs full of lighters, caps, and toys—3,200 km from the nearest city.

punchline.text: Our trash reaches the most remote places—and the most innocent creatures.

quiz.question: What percentage of seabirds now have plastic in their stomachs?
